title: Digital access is a practical consumer and civic bottleneck for Canadians with disabilities
source_unit: Statistics Canada Barriers to Accessibility in Canada: Communication and Internet Use, 2022, with 2024 Survey Series on Accessibility technology measures
geography: Canada; persons aged 15 years and older with disabilities or long-term conditions

denominator.unit: Canadians aged 15 years and older with one or more disabilities, approximate published population frame

communication_barriers.unit: percent experiencing communication barriers at least sometimes in the previous 12 months

internet_use_barriers.unit: percent experiencing Internet-use barriers at least sometimes in the previous 12 months

government_online_barrier.unit: percent experiencing barriers accessing government information, services, or supports online

booking_online_barrier.unit: percent experiencing barriers booking appointments, services, or reservations online

banking_shopping_online_barrier.unit: percent experiencing barriers while banking or shopping online

severity_gradient.value: Internet-use barriers: 28% among people with very severe disabilities versus 9% among people with mild disabilities; 47% among people with four or more disability types versus 8% with one

mechanism.value: Digital access is not only a communications issue: it is a gate into public services, appointments, banking, shopping, consumer remedy, and civic participation

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Statistics Canada’s 2022 Canadian Survey on Disability release; respondents reporting barriers sometimes, often, or always are classified as experiencing a barrier at least sometimes.
observations.uncertainty: The barriers are self-reported and cover selected situations rather than all accessibility barriers. This is cross-sectional evidence and does not establish service failure, financial loss, consumer exit, or causal effects of disability severity.
observations.subgroup: Canadians aged 15 years and older with one or more disabilities, compared across severity, number of disability types, income, age, and selected identity groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A reported barrier may be intermittent or overcome through assistance, alternate channels, or adaptation; a low percentage does not mean an accessible or equitable service system.

observations.period: 2024; technology-device and online communication barriers among persons with disabilities or long-term conditions

denominator.unit: Canadian persons with disabilities or long-term conditions participating in the 2024 Survey Series on Accessibility – Experiences with Accessibility and Information and Communication Technology

device_difficulty.unit: percent experiencing difficulty using a technological device such as a smartphone or laptop during the preceding three months

cellphone_barrier.unit: percent experiencing a cellphone-use barrier during the preceding three months

online_communication_barrier.unit: percent experiencing a barrier while performing communication-related activities online

online_support_barrier.unit: percent reporting difficulty accessing support services through communication-related tools

online_time_limit_barrier.unit: percent reporting time limits to complete actions on communication-related tools

mechanism.value: The practical bottleneck can occur inside ordinary interfaces—installation, touchscreens, adjustable settings, support access, and time limits—so nominal digital availability is not equivalent to usable access

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from Statistics Canada’s 2024 Survey Series on Accessibility – Experiences with Accessibility and Information and Communication Technology measures as summarized in the official release.
observations.uncertainty: The SSA-EAICT is a cross-sectional probability-panel survey of people identified through the 2022 CSD, with low cumulative response rate and possible non-response bias. Measures refer to barriers experienced because of a condition and do not quantify unsuccessful transactions, costs, complaint outcomes, or remedy.
observations.subgroup: Canadian persons with disabilities or long-term conditions identified under the 2024 survey’s condition framework.
observations.counterinterpretation: Technology barriers may be mitigated by assistive devices, help from others, alternate channels, or provider accommodation; the measures do not show whether a person completed a task or exited a service.

related_sources.claim: Statistics Canada detailed communication-barrier report from the 2022 Canadian Survey on Disability.
Canadian Survey on Disability program and methodological route.
Survey Series on Accessibility – Experiences with Accessibility and Information and Communication Technology program and cross-sectional probability-panel caveats.
Statistics Canada infographic route for technology-related barriers faced by persons with disabilities or long-term conditions in 2024.

boundary: This record adds an accessibility-to-consumer/civic-access layer. It does not establish digital exclusion as a universal condition, transaction failure, lost income, service-remedy performance, cultural participation, or causal effects; 2022 CSD and 2024 SSA-EAICT are distinct cross-sectional frames.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official Statistics Canada release reviewed for 2022 communication and Internet-use barriers, severity and income gradients, online government/booking/banking/shopping situations, and 2024 device and online-communication barriers; survey design and non-response cautions retained.
